chunks: And by this chain of narration, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, and Bukayr — they said: We heard Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) say:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to perform voluntary (supererogatory) prayers equal to twice the obligatory prayers, and fast voluntarily equal to twice the obligatory fast.

key_terms.التَّطَوُّعِ: tathawwu' — voluntary/supererogatory worship; acts of worship performed beyond the obligatory minimum, out of willing devotion
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: farida — the prescribed obligatory duty; binding acts of worship required of every Muslim (here: obligatory prayers and fasts)
key_terms.مِثْلَيِ: dual of mithl (measure/like) — 'twice the amount'; the Prophet's supererogatory acts equalled double the obligatory

ai.seo_question: How much did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) perform voluntary prayers and fasts beyond the obligatory duties according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Three companions of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) jointly report that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) performed supererogatory (tathawwu') prayers amounting to twice the obligatory prayers, and likewise fasted voluntarily to twice the measure of the obligatory fast. This hadith underscores the Prophet's extraordinary personal devotion beyond the minimum prescriptions, transmitted by the Imam as a model of prophetic conduct.
word_analysis: may God's blessings be upon him and his family (SAWW)
